prompt.context: We have a private equity client that is considering purchasing a small company that makes paintball guns called Splat. Sales last year were $50M, net profit was $20M, and they have been growing at 50% per year. The client has asked us for help in evaluating this investment. You and I are the team members who will do the bulk of the thinking and analysis.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate whether or not this paintball gun company (Splat) is a good investment?

clarifying_info.q: Are there any secondary research reports on the paintball gun market?
clarifying_info.a: No, there are no secondary research reports on the paintball gun market. You will need to estimate it yourselves.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of the population plays paintball?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of the population plays paintball in a given year.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of players actually purchase a gun rather than rent?
How many guns does the average purchaser buy per year?
What is the average price of a paintball gun?
How fast is the paintball market growing?
clarifying_info.a: The market is growing approximately 20% per year and will continue to do so for the next several years.

clarifying_info.q: How do customers perceive Splat relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: When surveyed, customers indicated they buy based on reputation for quality, and Splat is known as having the best paintball guns on the market. Two other players are viewed quite favorably, but not as highly ranked as Splat.

clarifying_info.q: Through what channels does Splat sell?
clarifying_info.a: Splat sells through paintball specialty stores and large chains such as Galyans, Sports Authority, and Wal-Mart. Sales have been steady through the specialty channel but growing ~60% per year in large chains.

clarifying_info.q: Are the large chain stores themselves growing faster than competitors' stores?
clarifying_info.a: No. Store managers consistently said sales were growing at 20% across all brands; Splat was doing slightly better than others at ~25% growth.

clarifying_info.q: Why are large chain sales growing 60% for Splat specifically?
clarifying_info.a: Over the last few years, the chains have been adding Splat to a few new store locations per year. They are now in almost all of the stores, so this roll-out is essentially complete.

framework: Assess market attractiveness: size the paintball gun market, estimate growth rate, and evaluate structural attractiveness
Assess Splat's competitive position: product quality, brand perception, customer loyalty, and market share
Understand the drivers of Splat's 50% growth vs. 20% market growth — identify whether growth is sustainable
Evaluate the deal valuation and price paid relative to projected future cash flows and growth
Identify key risks to the investment thesis

questions.prompt: Size the US paintball gun market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a bottom-up estimate using population, participation rate, purchase rate, frequency, and price. Should arrive at approximately $300M and note that Splat's $50M in sales implies ~17-20% market share.

math.setup: Annual market size = US population × paintball participation rate × gun purchase rate × guns per purchaser × average gun price
math.answer: ~$300M market; Splat has approximately 17-20% market share

questions.prompt: Is the paintball gun market attractive, and is the growth rate sustainable?
questions.guidance: Market is growing ~20% per year. Candidate should suggest methods for estimating growth (surveying participants, calling retailers, analyzing demographic trends). Should recognize that Splat's 50% growth outpaces the 20% market growth, implying Splat is gaining share.

questions.prompt: What explains the gap between Splat's 50% growth and the market's 20% growth?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies three compounding drivers: (1) high underlying market growth (~20%), (2) quality/brand advantage leading to slight share gain (~25% in existing stores), (3) distribution expansion — Splat being added to large chain stores in recent years accounts for the majority of the 50% vs. 20% gap. Candidate should probe both end-consumer perception and retail channel dynamics. Key insight: the distribution roll-out is now largely complete (Splat is in almost all chain stores), so future growth will revert toward 20-25%.

brainstorming.prompt: The market is growing at 20% and Splat has a slightly better product than competitors. What else could explain Splat growing at 50% vs. the 20% market rate?

categories.name: Distribution / Channel expansion
ideas: Splat recently added to large national chain stores (Galyans, Sports Authority, Wal-Mart)
New store locations opened by chain retailers
Increased shelf space or placement within existing stores

categories.name: Product / Brand
ideas: Splat perceived as best quality — attracts customers switching from competitors
New product launches or SKUs appealing to broader demographics

categories.name: Marketing & Pricing
ideas: Promotional pricing in new retail channels

categories.name: Market dynamics
ideas: Splat's channels (large chains) are growing faster than specialty channels where competitors are concentrated
Entry into adjacent markets (corporate events, birthday parties, military training)

recommendation: The investment appears attractive: Splat operates in a high-growth market (~20% per year), holds the leading quality position in the eyes of consumers, and has demonstrated the ability to gain share in existing stores (~25% growth in-store).

However, the extraordinary 50% growth was primarily driven by a one-time distribution roll-out into large chain stores, which is now essentially complete. Future growth should be modeled at 20-25% per year, not 50%.
Whether to proceed depends on the price the client is paying — the valuation must be justified by 20-25% annual growth, not the recent 50% headline.
risks: Paintball participation may be a fad; if participation rates decline, the entire market shrinks
Brand perceptions can shift quickly; Splat's quality advantage is not guaranteed to persist
Safety incidents (injuries or fatalities) could reduce participation across the industry or create direct legal liability for Splat
With the retail roll-out complete, Splat loses its primary growth lever — any slowdown below 20% would disappoint
Competitive response: well-funded competitors could replicate Splat's quality or undercut on price
next_steps: Negotiate deal price based on 20-25% growth assumption, not 50%
Conduct deeper due diligence on product defensibility (patents, manufacturing barriers to entry)
Model downside scenario where market growth slows to 10% or below
Explore whether further international distribution could replace the exhausted domestic channel expansion lever
Assess legal/liability exposure from product safety
